## Versions
- C23 | The reference treats C23 as the most recently published C Standard, so it is the main focus. (https://en.cppreference.com/Cppreference:About)
- C standard revisions | The reference covers C89, C95, C99, C11, C17 and C23. (https://en.cppreference.com/)

# osdev-core
## APIs
- LIDT | The instruction loads the IDTR from a pointer to an IDT descriptor made of a 16-bit Size and an Offset. Offset is 4 bytes in 32-bit mode and 8 bytes in 64-bit mode. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- IDT gate descriptor | A 32-bit entry is 8 bytes. It holds an ISR offset split in two parts, a code-segment selector, a gate type, a DPL and a present bit. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- struct InterruptDescriptor32 | The page gives a C struct that starts with a `uint16_t offset_1` field and a `uint16_t selector` field. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- Page directory and page table | On 32-bit x86, each has 1024 four-byte entries, so each is 4 KiB. A directory entry points to a page table. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Paging)
- Round Robin scheduler | It uses one queue. When the system timer fires, it switches to the next process. Each process gets a quantum counted in timer ticks. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Scheduling_Algorithms)

## Pitfalls
- Set up a working GDT before the IDT. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- Any IDT entry that is not present causes a General Protection Fault when it is used. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- The IDTR Offset must be a linear address, not a physical one, because paging applies. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- The page table address in a directory entry must be 4 KiB aligned, because the low bits are used for flags. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Paging)
- The CPU never clears the Accessed bit, so the OS must clear it if it needs it. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Paging)
- To make a page a user page, set the user bit in both the directory entry and the table entry. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Paging)
- Plain Round Robin has no priorities, so many low-priority processes can starve a high-priority one. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Scheduling_Algorithms)
- A smaller quantum means more time spent on context switches. A larger one makes the system feel laggier. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Scheduling_Algorithms)

## Notes
- The IDT has 256 vectors, 0 to 255. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Interrupt_Descriptor_Table)
- Serial ports are much easier to write drivers for than USB, and they are commonly used for debugging in early kernel work. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Serial_Ports)
- QEMU and Bochs can redirect serial output to stdio or to a file. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Serial_Ports)
- On x86-64, paging fully replaces segmentation for memory protection. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Paging)
- The page lists a 20–50 ms quantum as a common compromise. (https://wiki.osdev.org/Scheduling_Algorithms)
